title: The One who started everything still adds as He wills.
subtitle: Praise for the Originator and His winged messengers
then: Ibn Abbas said he only understood the word Fatir when two bedouins argued over a well and one said, I started it. {idea}Allah is the One who started the heavens and the earth.{/idea} The angels carry His word between Him and His prophets, with wings to move quickly.
now: You open your phone and scroll past a photo of a galaxy, then a newborn, then a storm. You feel nothing much. {idea}Each one was started by Someone.{/idea} This verse begins with praise before it asks anything of you.
old: The world is just there, a backdrop to my day.
new: Everything I see was started on purpose, and its Maker can still add to it.
try: Step outside once today and look at one natural thing for ten seconds. Say alhamdulillah for it.

title: No door He opens can be shut by anyone.
subtitle: Mercy given and held back by one hand
then: The Prophet ﷺ used to say after prayer: {idea}O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold.{/idea} The verse gave the believers in Makkah, who were pressured from all sides, one place to look.
now: You are waiting for an email about the job. You refresh it again and again, as if the hiring manager holds your whole future. {reward}If it is written for you, no one can block it.{/reward} If it is held back, no one can force it open.
old: If I do not please the right people, I will lose what I need.
new: People are only the doors. The One who opens and closes them is Allah.
try: After your next prayer, say the words: O Allah, none can withhold what You give. Mean one specific worry.

title: Who else sends you rain and food?
subtitle: Remembering the favor leads to the One who gives it
then: Makkah lived on rain, trade, and what the land could give. Yet its people turned to idols. The verse asks them to {idea}remember the favor{/idea} and then asks plainly: {trap}how are you turned away?{/trap}
now: Payday comes and you thank your company, your skills, your side hustle. The food on the table, the water in the tap, the air in your chest arrived without a thank you. {idea}Remembering is the first step back.{/idea}
old: I earned what I have through my own work.
new: My work was the path, but every bit of provision came from Allah.
try: Before eating today, name where the food came from all the way back to rain. Then thank Allah.

title: You are not the first to be called a liar.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet when he was denied
then: The leaders of Makkah rejected the message of one God. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}the messengers before him brought the same message and were denied too.{/idea} The final word on all of it {reward}returns to Allah.{/reward}
now: You speak up about something right at work or in the family chat, and you are laughed at or ignored. You start to doubt yourself. {idea}Being rejected does not make you wrong.{/idea} The outcome is not yours to settle.
old: If people reject what I say, maybe I should stop.
new: Rejection is an old path. The result belongs to Allah, not to the crowd.
try: Think of one good thing you stopped doing because someone mocked it. Do it once today, quietly.

title: Two deceivers: this life and the one who whispers.
subtitle: The promise is true, so do not be fooled
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}this life is as nothing compared to what Allah has promised{/idea} to those who follow His messengers. The Deceiver is Shaytan, who wants people to {trap}treat the brief as if it were lasting.{/trap}
now: Late at night you are deep in a shopping app, building a cart for a life you think will finally feel complete. Tomorrow there will be another cart. {trap}The feed never says it is temporary.{/trap} {idea}The promise of Allah does.{/idea}
old: I will think about the next life once this one is sorted.
new: This life is the test, not the prize. The promise ahead is the real thing.
try: Delete one item from a wishlist or cart today and spend that thought on one lasting deed.

title: He is your enemy, so treat him as one.
subtitle: Shaytan invites only to the Blaze

row.title: an enemy's invitation
sub: oppose it, do not trust it

then: Ibn Kathir says Shaytan {trap}declared his enmity toward the children of Adam{/trap} when he refused to bow to Adam. So the believer is told to {idea}be even firmer against him{/idea} and not believe the things he dresses up as good.
now: The voice that says skip prayer, you are tired. The one that says one look will not hurt. {trap}It sounds friendly and reasonable.{/trap} {idea}Naming it as an enemy takes away half its power.{/idea}
old: Every thought in my head is mine and on my side.
new: Some whispers come from an enemy who wants me lost. I can refuse them.
try: The next time you hear a lazy or harmful whisper today, say a'udhu billah and do the opposite.

title: Two roads, two endings, set side by side.
subtitle: Denial and its punishment, faith with forgiveness
then: Right after warning about Shaytan's followers, the verse shows both endings. Ibn Kathir notes that believers get {reward}forgiveness for whatever sins they did{/reward} and {reward}a great reward for the good they did.{/reward}
now: You look back at last year and see mostly mistakes. You assume the door is closed. {reward}This verse puts forgiveness before the reward.{/reward} The road is faith and good deeds, not a spotless past.
old: I have messed up too much for any reward to be mine.
new: The believer's ending starts with forgiveness. My part is faith and doing good now.
try: Do one small good deed today with the intention that it is a fresh start.

title: When the wrong thing starts to look good.
subtitle: And do not let grief over others destroy you
then: Some in Makkah did wrong and believed they were doing right. The Prophet ﷺ was deeply saddened by it. Allah told him {idea}not to destroy himself in sorrow for them,{/idea} for {idea}Allah guides whom He wills with full knowledge and wisdom.{/idea}
now: Two things to check. First, the habit you defend with good reasons: {trap}has it been dressed up for you?{/trap} Second, the brother you have argued with for years. {idea}Your job is to care and speak, not to carry his heart.{/idea}
old: If someone I love does not change, I have failed them.
new: I can call and care, but guidance is in Allah's hands, not mine.
try: Make one sincere dua for someone you worry about, then put the worry down for today.

title: Dead ground turns green, and so will you rise.
subtitle: Rain on a dead land as a picture of the Resurrection
then: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ how Allah brings the dead back. He ﷺ asked him if he had not passed his people's valley {trap}dry and barren{/trap}, then seen it {reward}stirring and green.{/reward} That, he said, is how Allah brings the dead to life.
now: You drive past the empty lot in late summer, all brown and cracked. A few weeks after the rain, it is full of grass. {idea}You have seen a small resurrection many times without calling it that.{/idea}
old: Life after death is hard to picture, so I keep it vague.
new: Every greening after rain is a preview of the Day I will rise.
try: Next time it rains, watch a patch of ground for a moment and remember this verse.

title: Want honor? It all belongs to Allah.
subtitle: Good words rise, good deeds lift them, show-offs fade
then: Ibn Abbas explained that {reward}remembrance of Allah rises, and the deed carries it up.{/reward} Mujahid said those who plot evil are the show-offs who look obedient. {trap}Their plan fails and their reality comes out.{/trap}
now: You post the charity drive, the gym streak, the Quran page. The likes come in and feel like honor. {idea}Honor that lasts comes from what Allah sees, not what the feed sees.{/idea} The show eventually slips.
old: Being respected depends on how people see me.
new: All honor belongs to Allah. My words and deeds rise to Him, seen or unseen.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody will ever know about. Not even a hint.

title: Every pregnancy and every birthday is already known.
subtitle: From dust to a full or short life, all recorded
then: The verse traces people from the dust of Adam to pairs that find rest in each other. {idea}No woman conceives or gives birth without His knowledge.{/idea} Every life, long or short, {idea}is written in a register.{/idea}
now: A hospital corridor at 3 a.m. Someone is giving birth in one room and someone is fading in another. {idea}Neither is a surprise to Allah.{/idea} {reward}Your own days are counted with care, not by chance.{/reward}
old: Life and death feel random and out of control.
new: Every beginning and end is known and written by the One who finds it easy.
try: Call or message an elderly relative today and simply ask how they are.

title: Sweet river, salty sea, both feeding you.
subtitle: Two kinds of water, so that you may give thanks
then: Ibn Kathir describes the fresh rivers flowing among people {reward}according to their needs{/reward}, and the salty ocean where big ships sail for trade. Both give fish and pearls. {idea}All of it was made to serve people so they would give thanks.{/idea}
now: You turn on the tap, eat tuna from a can, and wait for a parcel shipped across an ocean. {idea}Three gifts of water before lunch.{/idea} The verse ends with perhaps you will be grateful.
old: Water, food, and shipping are just how the world works.
new: Each one is a favor placed in my path so I would thank the One behind it.
try: Drink a glass of water slowly today and thank Allah for it before and after.

title: They do not own even the skin of a date seed.
subtitle: The Lord of night and day versus false helpers
then: Allah {idea}lengthens the night from the day and the day from the night{/idea} through summer and winter, and keeps the sun and moon on their course. The idols of Makkah, by contrast, {trap}did not own even the thin thread on a date pit.{/trap}
now: You check the horoscope app, the lucky charm on the mirror, the influencer who promises success. {trap}None of them moved the sunrise this morning.{/trap} {idea}The One who did is your Lord.{/idea}
old: A little extra help from somewhere else cannot hurt.
new: Only the One who runs night and day owns anything. Everything else holds nothing.
try: Watch the sunrise or sunset once this week and remember who runs it on time.

title: They cannot hear you, and could not answer if they did.
subtitle: False helpers will disown you on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idols could not hear because they had no life in them. Even if they could, {trap}they could do nothing.{/trap} On the Day they will deny the worship given to them. {idea}None informs you like the All-Aware.{/idea}
now: In a crisis you call everyone in your contacts list before you raise your hands to Allah. {trap}Some do not pick up. Some cannot help.{/trap} {idea}He hears the first time, before you even say it.{/idea}
old: I will try every other option first and pray if nothing works.
new: Only Allah truly hears and answers. He should be my first call, not my last.
try: Next time something goes wrong today, make a short dua before you reach for your phone.

title: You are the ones in need. He needs nothing.
subtitle: All people stand in need before the Rich, the Praised
then: Addressed to all of mankind, the verse sets out the plain truth. Ibn Kathir says {idea}people need Him in all that they do, but He has no need of them at all.{/idea} He is praised in everything He does and decrees.
now: You pride yourself on not asking anyone for help. Then the Wi-Fi goes down, a tooth aches, the car will not start, and you feel how thin your independence is. {idea}Need is not weakness. It is your true position.{/idea}
old: Needing help means I am weak or failing.
new: I am always in need of Allah, and admitting it is the start of strength.
try: Make one dua today that begins: O Allah, I am in need of You for this.

title: He could replace you with a new creation.
subtitle: Allah does not need us to stay

row.title: Allah needs my worship
sub: I am doing Him a favor

then: Right after saying all people are in need of Him, the verse adds a sobering line. Ibn Kathir says {idea}if He wanted, He could remove them and bring forth another people.{/idea} The Makkans were not indispensable to Him.
now: You sometimes pray as if you are doing Allah a favor, keeping score of your good weeks. {trap}As if He would be lost without you.{/trap} {idea}Being kept here is the gift.{/idea} Your worship benefits you.
old: My prayers and good deeds are something Allah needs from me.
new: Allah needs nothing from me. Being allowed to worship Him is the gift.
try: Before your next prayer, thank Allah for still giving you the chance to stand before Him.

title: Not hard for Him at all.
subtitle: What feels impossible to us is easy for Allah
then: This short verse closes the thought before it. Ibn Kathir says replacing the people {idea}is not difficult or impossible for Him.{/idea} It reminded the proud leaders of Makkah that their position was held up by nothing of their own.
now: You stare at a problem that feels like a mountain: the debt, the diagnosis, the son who will not talk to you. {idea}What is impossible for you is not hard for Him.{/idea} The same truth that humbles you also comforts you.
old: Some things in my life are just too big to ever change.
new: Nothing is hard for Allah. The size of my problem is measured by my strength, not His.
try: Name your biggest stuck problem in a dua today and add: and this is easy for You.

title: No one will carry your load for you.
subtitle: Each person carries their own burden on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir explains that even a father or son will refuse to carry any part of another's load, {trap}for each person will be preoccupied with his own self.{/trap} The warning only helps those who fear their Lord unseen and pray. {reward}Whoever purifies himself does it for himself.{/reward}
now: You lean on your mother's prayers, your spouse's religiousness, the pious uncle in the family. {trap}You assume some of it rubs off.{/trap} {idea}Your own heart is the one you are responsible for.{/idea}
old: My family is religious, so I am probably fine.
new: Their goodness is theirs. I carry my own load, and my own effort helps me.
try: Pick one small habit to clean up this week, for your own soul, not for anyone else.

title: The blind and the seeing are not the same.
subtitle: The first of four pairs that cannot be equal

key.label: Is it all the same in the end?

then: Allah uses opposites everyone in Makkah understood. Ibn Kathir says {idea}there is a huge gap between the blind and the seeing.{/idea} This is a parable: {reward}the believer sees{/reward}, while the one who rejects the truth walks without sight.
now: You know people who see the same headlines, the same deaths, the same signs, and feel nothing. You have days like that too. {idea}Sight is a gift you can lose or sharpen.{/idea}
old: Believing or not, people mostly end up in the same place.
new: Seeing the truth and being blind to it are worlds apart, now and later.
try: Ask Allah today for clear sight: O Allah, show me the truth as truth.

title: Darkness and light are not the same.
subtitle: The second pair: where you walk
then: After the blind and the seeing comes darkness and light. Ibn Kathir links it to a verse about a person {reward}given a light to walk with among people{/reward}, compared with one {trap}in darkness he cannot leave.{/trap}
now: You wake up anxious, scroll the news in the dark, and feel lost before breakfast. Then you pray Fajr and something steadies. {idea}Faith is not just an idea. It is light to walk by.{/idea}
old: Faith is a private view that does not change much day to day.
new: Faith is light. It shows me the next step when everything else is dark.
try: Tomorrow, before checking your phone, read one verse or make one dhikr first.

title: Shade and burning heat are not the same.
subtitle: The third pair: where the road ends
then: People who lived under the Arabian sun knew exactly what shade meant. Ibn Kathir says the believer walks his path {reward}until he settles in Gardens with shade and springs{/reward}, while the other ends in {trap}hot wind with no relief.{/trap}
now: A July afternoon, waiting at a bus stop with no shelter, and then you step into a cool shop. {reward}You feel the difference in your whole body.{/reward} {idea}The verse wants the next life to feel that real.{/idea}
old: The Hereafter feels too far off to really picture.
new: The difference between shade and heat is something I already know. The next life is that real.
try: The next time you step into shade or cool air today, ask Allah for the shade of Paradise.

title: The living and the dead are not the same.
subtitle: Allah makes hear whom He wills
then: The final pair is the sharpest. The believers are the living and the deniers are like the dead. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah guides whom He wills to listen to the proof and accept it,{/idea} while the Prophet ﷺ {trap}could not make those in graves hear.{/trap}
now: You have sent the article, the video, the long voice note to your friend. Nothing lands. {idea}Hearts are opened by Allah, not by the perfect message.{/idea} Make sure your own heart is the living one.
old: If I explain it well enough, anyone will accept it.
new: Only Allah makes a heart hear. My job is to keep my own heart alive.
try: Read one verse slowly today and ask Allah to let your heart hear it.

title: You are only a warner.
subtitle: The Prophet's role: convey, not control
then: After saying the dead cannot be made to hear, Allah reassures the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Kathir says {idea}all he had to do was convey the message and warn them.{/idea} Guiding or leaving astray belongs to Allah.
now: You are the parent who has said the same reminder about prayer a hundred times. {trap}You feel like you are failing.{/trap} {idea}Even the Prophet ﷺ was told his role was to convey.{/idea} Say it kindly, then trust Allah with the rest.
old: If they do not change, I have done my job badly.
new: My job is to convey with care. The result was never in my hands.
try: Give one gentle reminder today with no lecture after it, then leave it with Allah.

title: Every nation had a warner pass through it.
subtitle: Sent with truth, good news, and warning
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was sent as {reward}a bearer of good news to believers{/reward} and a warner to deniers. And {idea}no nation of the children of Adam was left without warners{/idea}, so none had an excuse.
now: You tell yourself you never really learned your religion, that nobody taught you properly. {idea}Yet the message reached you, in this very card.{/idea} Glad news and warning both, delivered with care.
old: I was never properly taught, so it is not really on me.
new: The message has reached me. Now what I do with it is mine.
try: Learn the meaning of one short surah you recite in prayer this week.

title: They came with clear proofs and a light-giving Book.
subtitle: Earlier messengers were denied despite clear signs
then: The Prophet ﷺ is comforted again: earlier peoples denied too. Ibn Kathir says their messengers came with {reward}clear miracles and definitive proofs{/reward} and books that were plain. {trap}Still they denied.{/trap}
now: You say you would pray more if you were just more certain. Then you notice you already know enough to start. {trap}The missing piece is often not proof but will.{/trap} {idea}The light is already on the table.{/idea}
old: If I had more proof, I would commit more.
new: The proof is clear. What I lack is usually the will, not the evidence.
try: Do one act of worship today you have been putting off until you felt sure enough.

title: Then I seized them, and how severe it was.
subtitle: Denial after clear signs has an end

key.label: Is there no end to delay?

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}despite all the signs, they denied the messengers, so Allah seized them with punishment.{/trap} The verse asks the listener to think how great that reproach was, and to {idea}take warning while there is time.{/idea}
now: You keep a sin on repeat, telling yourself there is always tomorrow to fix it. {idea}The open door is mercy, not permission.{/idea} {reward}Turning back today is still possible.{/reward}
old: There will always be more time to turn things around.
new: The time to respond to the truth is now, while the door is still open.
try: Say astaghfirullah sincerely for one specific thing today and decide one step away from it.

title: One rain, a thousand colors.
subtitle: Fruits and mountains of many shades from one water
then: Ibn Kathir notes how Allah {idea}makes different kinds of things from one thing, the water from the sky.{/idea} Fruits come in countless colors, tastes, and scents. Even the mountains carry streaks of white, red, and deep black.
now: The market stall: red apples, yellow mangoes, green grapes, all grown on the same rainwater. {idea}You walk past it like it is normal.{/idea} {reward}It is a gallery.{/reward}
old: Color and variety in nature are just background.
new: Every shade from the same rain is a sign of the One who made it.
try: At your next meal, notice the colors on the plate and say subhanallah once for each.

title: The more you know Him, the more you fear Him.
subtitle: Colors in people and animals, and true knowledge

picture.label: Signs and those who read them

then: Humans and animals vary in color like fruits and mountains. Then the verse says only those with knowledge truly fear Allah. Sa'id bin Jubayr said {idea}fear is what stands between you and disobeying Allah.{/idea} {reward}And He is Oft-Forgiving.{/reward}
now: You can name every player in a league or every setting on your phone. {trap}Knowing lots of things does not change how you live.{/trap} {idea}Knowing Allah does.{/idea} It shows up when you are alone and could do wrong.
old: Knowledge means having lots of information.
new: Real knowledge is knowing Allah so well that it keeps me from sin.
try: Learn the meaning of one of Allah's names today and think of it once before sleeping.

title: A trade that can never go bust.
subtitle: Reciting, praying, and giving as an investment
then: Makkah was a trading city, and the Quran spoke its language. Ibn Kathir says those who recite and act on the Book, pray on time, and spend {reward}hope for a reward from Allah which will inevitably be theirs.{/reward}
now: You check the stocks, the crypto, the savings rate, worried about losses. {trap}Every one of those can drop.{/trap} {reward}A page of Quran, a prayer on time, a quiet donation do not crash.{/reward}
old: My real investments are the financial ones.
new: Reciting, praying, and giving are a trade with Allah that never loses.
try: Give a small amount in charity today, secretly, and think of it as an investment.

title: Paid in full, then given more.
subtitle: The Forgiving who appreciates even a little
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah pays them for what they did and {reward}multiplies it with more, such as has never occurred to them.{/reward} He is Forgiving of their sins and {idea}appreciates even a little of their good deeds.{/idea}
now: You gave five minutes to help a stranger with directions and forgot it by lunch. {idea}Allah did not forget.{/idea} {reward}The One who appreciates sees small things and repays them generously.{/reward}
old: My small good deeds are too little to matter.
new: Allah appreciates even a little, pays it in full, and adds more.
try: Do one tiny good deed today, like a smile or holding a door, and trust it counts.

title: The Book is the truth, confirming what came before.
subtitle: The Quran stands in a line of revelation
then: The Makkans called the message something new and strange. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that what was revealed to him {idea}is the very truth, confirming the books before it{/idea}, which had themselves pointed to its coming. {idea}Allah knows and sees His servants.{/idea}
now: You hold your phone with the Quran app open and treat it like one more piece of content. {idea}It is the same truth sent to every prophet, now in your hand.{/idea} The One who sent it sees you reading.
old: The Quran is one religious text among many I could pick from.
new: It is the truth that confirms all earlier revelation, sent by the One who sees me.
try: Open the Quran today and read just one page with full attention, phone on silent.

title: Three kinds of heirs, all chosen.
subtitle: Those who fall short, the moderate, and the foremost

row.title: I fall short, I am out

then: Ibn Kathir says this Ummah inherited the Book and is of three types. {idea}The correct view is that even those who wrong themselves are part of it.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said the foremost enter without account, and {reward}the others by mercy and intercession.{/reward}
now: You miss prayers, skip the Quran for weeks, and think the believers in this verse are other people. {idea}You were named too, first in the list.{/idea} {reward}Being included is the start. Moving up is the goal.{/reward}
old: Only the truly pious inherit the Book. I am not one of them.
new: I was chosen to inherit it too. The question is which of the three I grow into.
try: Add one extra good deed today that moves you one step toward the foremost.

title: Gardens to live in forever, adorned and dressed.
subtitle: What awaits those who inherited the Book
then: Right after naming the three kinds of heirs, the verse shows their home. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}the believer's ornaments will reach as far as his wudu reaches.{/reward} The Gardens are entered on the Day they meet Allah.
now: You stand at the sink before Maghrib, washing your hands, face, and feet in a hurry. {reward}Those same places will shine with ornaments.{/reward} {idea}Wudu is not a chore. It is dressing for later.{/idea}
old: Wudu is just a step I rush through before prayer.
new: Every wudu adorns me for a home that lasts forever.
try: Make your next wudu slowly and completely, thinking of each part as being adorned.

title: Praise to Allah, who took all our sorrow away.
subtitle: The first words of the people of Paradise

row.title: grief and fear
sub: of this world and the next

then: In Paradise the believers say praise belongs to Allah. Ibn Kathir explains the sorrow as {trap}every anxiety of the world and the Hereafter{/trap} now lifted. Ibn Abbas said {reward}He forgives their major sins and appreciates even the smallest good deeds.{/reward}
now: You lie awake at 2 a.m. with that heavy chest: money, health, the future of your kids. {idea}This verse is a promise that it ends.{/idea} {reward}One day the whole weight of worry is simply gone.{/reward}
old: Worry is just part of who I am. It will always be there.
new: There is a home where every grief is removed. My worry has an end date.
try: Tonight, name your heaviest worry in dua and end with: alhamdulillah, You will lift it.

title: A home where no tiredness ever touches you.
subtitle: Settled forever out of His grace, not earned

row.title: His grace
sub: deeds are the door, mercy the key

then: The people of Paradise say Allah settled them there {reward}out of His grace{/reward}, for their deeds were not equal to it. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}none enters Paradise by his deeds alone, not even him, unless Allah covers him with mercy.{/idea}
now: Sunday night, dreading the Monday alarm. Bone tired, mind fried, nowhere to rest. {reward}A home where neither body nor soul ever gets exhausted.{/reward} {idea}And the way in is mercy.{/idea}
old: Rest is something I will get once I have done enough.
new: Lasting rest is a gift of His grace. My deeds are how I ask for it.
try: Take five quiet minutes today to rest and say: O Allah, settle me in the home of no tiredness.

title: No dying and no relief for the ungrateful.
subtitle: The opposite ending, told plainly
then: Having described the people of Paradise, the verse turns to the other ending. Ibn Kathir says they will wish death would bring rest, but {trap}it will not come, nor will the punishment be lightened.{/trap} {idea}This is the recompense of every ungrateful one.{/idea}
now: You take blessing after blessing and rarely say thank you. {idea}Ungratefulness grows quietly.{/idea} {reward}The good news is that the door to gratitude and faith is open today, for you.{/reward}
old: Hell is a distant idea that has nothing to do with my daily habits.
new: Gratitude or ingratitude, practiced every day, is shaping my ending now.
try: Write down three blessings from today and thank Allah for each one before sleeping.

title: Did We not give you a life long enough?
subtitle: The plea to go back, and the answer
then: They will beg to return and do good. The reply: {idea}did you not live long enough to take a reminder?{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said Allah leaves no excuse for one who reaches sixty. Some early scholars said the warner here is {trap}grey hair{/trap}; others said the Messenger ﷺ.
now: You spot the first grey hair in the bathroom mirror and laugh it off. {idea}It is a warner too.{/idea} {reward}You are still here, still able to begin.{/reward} The plea in this verse is one you will never need to make.
old: I will get serious about my faith when I am older.
new: The time I have now is the time I was given. It is enough to change.
try: Pick one change you keep postponing to someday and do its first small step today.

title: He knows what is hidden in the sky and in your chest.
subtitle: Nothing unseen is hidden from Allah
then: Right after the plea of those who said they would do good if sent back, Allah says He {idea}knows all that is hidden and the secrets of hearts.{/idea} He knows whether a promise is sincere, and {idea}rewards or punishes each by his deeds.{/idea}
now: Nobody at work knows why you really volunteered for the project. Nobody at the mosque knows what you were thinking during the sermon. {idea}Allah does.{/idea} {reward}That is also comfort: He knows the good you could not show.{/reward}
old: As long as I look fine on the outside, it is fine.
new: Allah sees my intentions as clearly as my actions, the good and the hidden.
try: Before one task today, pause and fix your intention for Allah alone.

title: Each generation takes its turn on the earth.
subtitle: Successors, and what persistence adds
then: Ibn Kathir says people succeed one another, generation after generation. {trap}The longer someone persists in denial, the more he loses.{/trap} In contrast, {reward}the longer believers live and do good, the higher their rank.{/reward}
now: You moved into a flat someone else lived in, work a desk someone else had, and will hand both on. {idea}You are taking a turn.{/idea} {reward}Every extra year can add to your rank if you fill it with good.{/reward}
old: Getting older just means losing time.
new: Every year given to me is a chance to rise higher if I use it well.
try: On your next birthday or today, write one good habit you want this year to add.

title: Show me what they created.
subtitle: A challenge to every false partner
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask the idol worshippers three plain questions. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they had nothing of that, not even the skin of a date seed.{/trap} They were {trap}following their own whims and wishes{/trap}, promising each other comfort.
now: Your friends reassure each other that a certain habit is fine because everyone does it. {trap}Nobody can point to proof, just to each other.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks: show me where it came from.{/idea}
old: If enough people around me believe it, it must be okay.
new: A belief needs real proof, not people reassuring each other.
try: Pick one thing you do because everyone does it, and ask yourself honestly what it is based on.

title: He holds the heavens and earth in place.
subtitle: And He is patient and forgiving while He does
then: After the challenge to false gods, Allah shows His power: {idea}the heavens and earth stand by His command.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that He is Forbearing, for {reward}He sees His servants disobey, yet He is patient, gives them time, and conceals their faults.{/reward}
now: You wake up, the floor is still there, the sky has not fallen, and you sin a little by noon. {reward}Still the world holds.{/reward} {idea}That patience is a door held open for you.{/idea}
old: The world is stable on its own. Nothing holds it.
new: Allah holds everything in place, and His patience with me is part of that mercy.
try: Look up at the sky once today and say: You hold it, and You are patient with me.

title: They swore they would follow, then they ran.
subtitle: Promised guidance, then aversion when it came

row.title: before
sub: send us a warner, we will follow

then: Before the Prophet ﷺ came, Quraysh and the Arabs {idea}swore their strongest oaths{/idea} that if a warner came they would be better guided than any nation. {trap}When he came, they only fled further.{/trap}
now: You said you would start praying properly once you finished exams, then once you got the job, then once you were married. {trap}Each time the moment came, you found a new reason.{/trap} {idea}The moment is the one you are in.{/idea}
old: When conditions are right, I will finally commit.
new: Promises about later are easy. Faith shows when the moment actually arrives.
try: Recall one if-only promise you made to Allah and keep a small part of it today.

title: The evil plot circles back to the one who made it.
subtitle: Arrogance, scheming, and Allah's unchanging way
then: Ibn Kathir explains they fled from the truth out of {trap}arrogance{/trap} and plotted to stop others from Allah's path. {idea}The evil consequences come back on them, not on others.{/idea} Allah's way with such people {idea}does not change or turn aside.{/idea}
now: You set someone up at work, quietly bend the story to make them look bad. It feels clever. {trap}Then you are the one who cannot sleep, cannot be trusted, has to keep the lie straight.{/trap} {idea}The plot always has a return address.{/idea}
old: If I am smart about it, a little scheming will work out for me.
new: Scheming against others always circles back to the one who schemes.
try: If you are holding a quiet plan against someone, drop it today. Replace it with a dua for them.

title: Go and look at how the stronger ones ended.
subtitle: Past nations were mightier, and none escaped Him
then: Makkan traders passed the ruins of older nations on their journeys. Ibn Kathir says to look how {trap}their homes were emptied after luxury, numbers, wealth, and children.{/trap} None of it helped. {idea}Nothing in the heavens or earth escapes Allah.{/idea}
now: You walk through an old part of the city where grand buildings now stand empty, or scroll a history page about a fallen empire. {trap}They felt permanent too.{/trap} {idea}Ask what you are really leaning on.{/idea}
old: With enough resources, I am safe.
new: The strongest before me could not escape Allah. My only safety is in Him.
try: Next time you pass something old or ruined, pause and ask what you will leave behind.

title: If He punished at once, nothing would be left.
subtitle: The respite until an appointed term
then: Fatir closes here. If Allah punished people for all they earned at once, {trap}He would leave no creature on the earth{/trap}; Sa'id bin Jubayr said He would hold back the rain. {reward}But He delays until an appointed term,{/reward} and He sees His servants fully.
now: Your mistakes from this week did not bring the sky down. The rain still came, the shop still opened, your heart still beats. {reward}That is not because no one saw. It is respite.{/reward} {idea}Use it.{/idea}
old: Since nothing bad happened, maybe it did not matter.
new: The delay is mercy and time to return, not a sign that Allah did not see.
try: Use today's respite well: make tawbah for one thing and do one good deed in its place.
